title: The Last Spire
premise: Gideon Blackwood has survived nine years as the king's food-taster by knowing exactly what to swallow and what to hide, and he knows the Thornfell smuggler roads better than any soldier alive. When a feral child appears at his door speaking the dead tongue of the Thornkings, Gideon discovers the child is a fragment of the mountain's old magic — and that the king has been hollowed out and worn as a vessel by the Spires, ancient parasites of the crown line. Hunted by the royal guard, guided by the child, and betrayed by the mentor who trained him, Gideon must carry the child through the smuggler roads to the Last Spire before the winter solstice, when the binding will become permanent. He ends the parasite's reign at the cost of his own immunity — and his own name — inheriting a guardianship he never wanted but cannot abandon.
about_author: Theo Reyes is the pen name of a former line cook turned fantasy novelist who swears his years tasting questionable stews inspired his fascination with poison, power, and who gets to eat. He writes in a mountain cabin with an unreasonable number of maps pinned to the walls.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A routine tasting in the royal kitchens turns deadly when Gideon detects nightshade in the king's wine — but the king drinks it anyway and does not die. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in Gideon's carefully ordered world, and a hint the king is not what he seems.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A mud-caked child appears at Gideon's cottage door, speaking a language no living scholar knows — yet Gideon half-understands it, a legacy of his grandmother's forbidden lullabies. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness awakening in a man trained to trust no one.

chapters.title: What the Wine Did Not Kill
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Court physician Maren examines the child and finds markings matching carvings in the sealed Thornking crypt. The king's guards arrive asking questions about the tainted wine. Emotional beat: dread tightening; Gideon realizes the child is a message someone died to send.

chapters.title: The Roads I Was Never Supposed to Know
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Fleeing the capital through smuggler passes only he knows, Gideon teaches the child survival while she teaches him fragments of the old tongue. Emotional beat: growing bond; for the first time, loyalty has a face instead of a seal.

chapters.title: The Hollow King
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. Inside the palace, we see the king's mind flickering — moments of the man he was surfacing beneath the thing that wears him, screaming soundlessly. Emotional beat: horror and pity; the antagonist is also a victim.

chapters.title: Salt and Silver
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the free-town of Bracken Hollow, smuggler queen Vessa recognizes the child's markings and offers passage — for a price Gideon cannot yet name. Emotional beat: wary negotiation; trust as currency, and every coin counterfeit.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Shadow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Corvin, the old spymaster who trained Gideon, catches up to them — not to arrest him, but to beg him to turn back, revealing he has served the Spires for thirty years. Emotional beat: betrayal; the father-figure revealed as the cage.

chapters.title: Lullabies of the Thornkings
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Gideon's translation). The child, Wren, remembers being part of the mountain's magic, split apart when the Spires first bound a king. Emotional beat: grief; inheritance as a wound passed down generations.

chapters.title: Vessa's Price
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Vessa names her price: the Last Spire's vault, where her family's stolen name is recorded. Gideon agrees, knowing the vault may not survive what he must do there. Emotional beat: complicity; every ally costs something he'll regret.

chapters.title: The Pass That Eats Travelers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A blizzard traps them in the Corpse Pass; Corvin's hunters close in, and Gideon must choose between a hidden route that may kill Wren and a fight he cannot win. Emotional beat: desperation; survival priced in blood.

chapters.title: What Immunity Is Worth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Wounded and feverish, Gideon's built-up immunities begin failing — the poisons he swallowed for the crown are turning on him. Maren, who followed them, treats him and confesses she poisoned the wine as a test. Emotional beat: reckoning; his body is a ledger of the crown's sins.

chapters.title: The King Remembers Snow
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. A childhood memory breaks through the parasite's grip for one full hour; Aldric writes a hidden letter and hides it in the crypt, a message only someone who knows the old tongue could find. Emotional beat: fragile hope flickering inside a dying man.

chapters.title: The Crypt Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Guided by Wren's songs, they breach the Thornking crypt and find Aldric's letter and a map to the Last Spire — plus evidence every king for three centuries has been bound. Emotional beat: revelation; the kingdom itself is the parasite's body.

chapters.title: Corvin's Confession
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Corvin corners them at the crypt mouth and, instead of fighting, kneels — he bound the first king as a young idealist believing it would end the wars. Emotional beat: tragic recognition; Gideon sees his own future in a man who chose order over truth.

chapters.title: The Hunt on the High Ridge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The royal guard, now fully the Spires' instrument, ambushes the party on the ridge. Vessa's smugglers hold the line; Maren is captured. Emotional beat: sacrifice; loyalty proven in wounds, not words.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. The parasite, sensing the endgame, rides Aldric's body out of the palace toward the Spire itself, devouring the last of the king's memories to fuel the solstice binding. Emotional beat: accelerating horror; the clock is now audible.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final climb to the Last Spire through the mountain's living passages, Wren growing stronger and more transparent as they near — she is returning to the whole she was cut from. Emotional beat: bittersweet anticipation; the mission's success is also a farewell.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Inside the Spire's vault, Vessa claims her family's name; Gideon finds his own grandmother's name among the bound guardians — his immunity was engineered, his whole life a preparation. Emotional beat: shattering inheritance; he was made for this and never asked.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the Spire's heart, Gideon faces the parasite wearing Aldric's body and begins the unbinding — Wren dissolving into the mountain's magic as the ritual demands a guardian's blood freely given. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity; love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: The King in the Snow
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. Freed, Aldric has hours left, not years; he abdicates in the snow outside the Spire, names Maren regent, and dies a man instead of a vessel. Emotional beat: catharsis; dignity reclaimed in the final hour.

chapters.title: The Taster Who Would Not Swallow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The new regency offers Gideon titles he refuses; his immunity is gone, his name struck from the rolls, and he is free. He takes Wren — reborn as an ordinary child — to Bracken Hollow. Emotional beat: quiet joy; survival finally without price.

chapters.title: The Last Spire Stands
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, epilogue. Years later, Gideon runs a roadside inn at the mountain's foot, feeding travelers freely. On solstice nights, the Spire glows faintly, and he climbs to keep the old vigil. Emotional beat: earned peace; inheritance accepted, guardianship chosen at last.
